newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Pedestrian New Zealand share market ends flat.
newsitem.headline: Pedestrian New Zealand share market ends flat.

text.p: * NZ top 40 index square after accounting for ex div stocks
* Market expecting uneventful week
* Tranz Rail rises after first quarter result
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
324 +4 * NZSC cap index -9.95 at 4,799.90
372 +5 * Volume $49 million. Futures untraded
737 -2 * Other movers - +17 -9
The New Zealand share market strolled to a flat finish on Monday and brokers are expecting holidays overseas and the U.S. election to keep the market tame for most of the week.
"It was pedestrian pace through most of the day," said Hendry Hay McIntosh broker Tim Koller.
The top 40 index closed 7.9 points off at 2,314.5, the fall almost precisely matching the effect of Brierley Investments and other stocks going ex-dividend.
Brierley shed a five cent dividend but ended seven down at $1.23 as the company continues to suffer fallout from the mediocre listing performance of Thistle Hotels in Britain.
Telecom also fell a couple of cents, to $7.37, while number two stock Carter Holt Harvey gained four to $3.24.
Carter is due to report its half year on Thursday and brokers said investors had factored in a predicted slump in earnings to $115-125 million from $271 million.

Star performer for the day was Tranz Rail which gained 17 cents to $7.90 but on very slim volume. It reported after the market closed on Friday and the result was in line, or slightly below expectations.

Monday's turnover included a line of over two million Fletcher Energy crossed on Friday. Brokers said the stock, which closed up two at $4.08, was still responding to a positive recommendation by HSBC James Capel.
